mechanism_narrative: The slight week-on-week increase in RETAIL_REC mobility observed in the most recent period indicates a nascent recovery trend, which will continue to lift retail and recreation activity over the next four weeks as people cautiously resume non-essential outings.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the average of the last 28 days, despite the recent uptick.

mechanism_narrative: The persistent and accelerating decline in TRANSIT station mobility indicates a reduction in overall public movement and commuting, which will suppress retail and recreation activity further over the next two weeks as fewer people travel for leisure or work-related shopping.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls by more than 1.0 percentage point week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is higher than the average of the last 14 days, despite TRANSIT continuing to fall by more than 1.0 percentage point week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in WORKPLACES mobility and a decrease in RESIDENTIAL mobility signals a shift in daily routines where more people are leaving their homes for work and other activities, directly boosting retail and recreation visits over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises by >1.0 percentage point AND RESIDENTIAL falls by >1.0 percentage point week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not increase, even when WORKPLACES rises and RESIDENTIAL falls concurrently by the specified thresholds.

mechanism_narrative: The sustained high level of RESIDENTIAL mobility, consistently above 25% from baseline, indicates that significant stay-at-home policies or strong public health advisories remain in effect, which will continue to suppress non-essential retail and recreation activity over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days increases significantly (more than 5 percentage points), despite RESIDENTIAL mobility remaining above 25% from baseline.

mechanism_narrative: The recent uptick in PARKS mobility, following a period of decline, suggests an increasing comfort level with outdoor activities. This trend will likely spill over into other leisure activities, leading to a modest increase in RETAIL_REC over the next one week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by more than 0.5 percentage points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days decreases or remains flat, despite a week-on-week increase in PARKS mobility exceeding 0.5 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: The overall extremely low levels of mobility across most categories (RETAIL_REC, GROCERY_PHARM, PARKS, WORKPLACES) indicate a deeply entrenched pattern of reduced movement, suggesting that this inertia will continue to keep RETAIL_REC suppressed over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days shows a significant increase (more than 5 percentage points) from the average of the last 28 days, despite all listed proxies remaining below -60% from baseline.

mechanism_narrative: Even as essential GROCERY_PHARM mobility remains relatively stable, the continued decline in TRANSIT station visits suggests a broader reluctance or inability to travel, which will negatively impact non-essential RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls by >1.0 percentage point week-on-week AND GROCERY_PHARM changes by <1.0 percentage point week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days increases, despite TRANSIT falling and GROCERY_PHARM remaining stable within the specified thresholds.

mechanism_narrative: The simultaneous minor upticks in RETAIL_REC, GROCERY_PHARM, PARKS, and WORKPLACES in the most recent week, following a period of decline, indicate a collective behavioral shift towards cautiously resuming more activities, which will lead to a small but sustained increase in RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days decreases or remains flat, despite concurrent minor upticks (at least 0.5 percentage points) in the specified mobility categories in the preceding week.
